youtube.title: A Navy Ship Vanished With 306 Aboard. No Wreck Was Ever Found. | USS Cyclops
youtube.description:
In March 1918, the US Navy collier USS Cyclops left Barbados for Baltimore carrying about 11,000 tons of manganese ore from Brazil, with 306 people aboard. She was reportedly overloaded and had a cracked cylinder in one engine. She never arrived, and no wreckage, bodies or distress call were ever found. It remains the US Navy's largest loss of life not directly involving combat. Leading explanations: structural failure in a storm (her sister ships Proteus and Nereus also later vanished), or sabotage by her German-born captain, George Worley, which German records do not support.

📂 Case File #025: The USS Cyclops

Sources: History (UK), "What happened to the USS Cyclops?"; Marine Insight, "The Story of USS Cyclops"; Wikipedia, "USS Cyclops (AC-4)" and its citations (Naval History and Heritage Command).
